advisories.title: The unrestorable-bytes record carries a byte count that no live artifact sources
advisories.detail: observedUnrestorableV1Reject.observedAs reads 'Claude REJECT 0/1 CLAUDE-FCRO-V1-SF1 at 29566 bytes'. The digest and the verdict characterisation are both traceable — my turn-2 verdict at aea22602 records them, as does the frozen v2 subject at 921bd720 and the turn-2 dispatch. The byte count is not: I grepped the corpus and 29566 appears in this artifact and in unrelated retention-tiers files, and specifically not in my turn-2 verdict. I can corroborate it from my own contemporaneous measurement of that path during the turn-2 cycle, and it is correct, but a later reviewer with no session memory has no way to check it and the artifact offers no provenance. Since the bytes are unrestorable by construction, this is the one datum here that can never be re-derived. Either cite claudeV2Reject as the provenance for the whole observation and drop the count, or keep it and mark it observed-not-reproducible. This does not affect any obligation, coverage or routing, which is why it is an advisory.

advisories.title: Four turn-1 advisories carry forward unchanged, because the fourteen states are byte-identical across all three turns
advisories.detail: (1) doctor v4's consent variant is grammatically ambiguous about whether the consent dimension crosses the other variants; the catalog takes the standalone-limb reading, which I judge correct and which the turn-1 dispatch endorsed, without recording that it took a reading. (2) The per-state NOT-AUTHORED markers are uneven — treeImage on the seven degraded states only, reportBytes on the two audit-write-fails states only — although all three pinned artifacts are equally absent for all fourteen. (3) g12v2.role still says 'v4 is a later subject under review'; I re-measured and G12 v4 now carries a Claude ACCEPT at 0/0, so that clause has been stale since before turn 1 closed, though the operative claim that v4 is not this catalog's pin remains correct. (4) FC-RO's governing pass property is carried nowhere while the variant-specific one is carried twice — defensible for an initial-state catalog, and worth noting only because that property's scope limb is what makes DEG-7 concurrent mutation scorable rather than a second grant-journal-style collision.

advisories.title: Three turns in, there is still no finding-disposition block, and the advisory set has now accumulated to seven items with no adopt-or-decline record
advisories.detail: Each turn has folded its binding finding cleanly and said nothing about the non-binding ones. Advisories are non-binding and silence is lawful, but this corpus has the idiom — doctor-actor-leftover-join.v2 carries a findingDisposition block naming each inherited item and its disposition — and the value of that idiom rises with each turn. A short block recording which advisories were considered and set aside, and why, would let the next reviewer and the recording D-000 see the difference between deliberate and overlooked. This is the one thing I would most like to see in a v4, if a v4 is authored for any other reason; it is not a reason to author one.

independence.priorParticipation: DISCLOSED AND MATERIAL, across all three turns. I raised CLAUDE-FCRO-V1-SF1 against v1 and CLAUDE-FCRO-V2-B1 against v2, and this verdict accepts the fold of the second. Three controls against marking my own homework. First, every repair was resolved against the ORIGINAL source — doctor v4's own bytes for the variant strings, the live v1 review path for its verdict and for the absence of the finding id — never against the candidate's account. Second, I re-derived the turn-1 and turn-2 conclusions this cycle instead of carrying them forward, including all five inherited standings, because a verdict file in this lineage moved under me once. Third, I held the two advisories I had previously declined to escalate at advisory rather than converting a clean fold into a fresh rejection; the reasoning for declining has not changed, and changing it now would be goalpost-moving rather than review. My own turn-2 verdict at aea22602 is intact and reproduces.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with four advisories. Thirteen attacks run, one landed and only at advisory grade. Custody holds in every direction the dispatch names: subject 19b7c129 at 0444, 15213 bytes, unmoved and unedited at both ends; the frozen v1 subject at 70877c0d; the live v1 review path at 65fef261, 0444, read but not overwritten; the frozen v2 subject at 921bd720; my own turn-2 verdict at aea22602, intact; HEAD never left 5d5d778; file 08 matches the subject's pin; required-now is 26 of 26. Eleven of eleven cited digests reproduce — the attack that landed at turn 2 does not land here. The blocker is fully repaired, and repaired the harder way. The broken claudeV1Reject entry is removed rather than amended; claudeV1ReviewLive pins the live 65fef261 and states three things about those bytes that all verify — ACCEPT at 0/0/0, mode 0444, and zero occurrences of CLAUDE-FCRO-V1-SF1. The candidate does not deny or withdraw that ACCEPT. The 49988c67 bytes are recorded as an observation under digestObservedThen with standing UNRESTORABLE and, importantly, with no path member, so the record cannot be misread as a live citation; I walked every field containing that string and all three frame it as observed-then or unrestorable. The false 'Claude REJECT 0/1' characterisation is gone from predecessorV1.role, and authorityClaim and purpose no longer claim to be landing a v1 REJECT. Best of all, the candidate expressly declines to settle which of the two v1 verdicts is the record — 'Coordinator disposition of competing v1-review observations is not performed here' — which is the correct division of authority and the part I was least confident would land. The turn-1 repair is preserved: variantsVerbatim[3] is 560 of 560 characters against live v4, re-derived this cycle. Nothing regressed — all fourteen states and every substantive block are byte-identical to v2, three paths removed, twelve added, five values changed, and the change set is exactly the blocker. Four advisories, none binding. The one new item: 'at 29566 bytes' in the unrestorable-bytes record is sourced by no live artifact — the digest and verdict characterisation are traceable to my turn-2 verdict, the byte count is not, and since those bytes are unrestorable by construction it is the one datum here that can never be re-derived; it is correct, and it should either cite its provenance or be marked observed-not-reproducible. The other three carry forward: the two per-state verbatimFromV4 prefixes, which I have now held at advisory three turns running on unchanged reasoning; the four turn-1 items that survive because the states are byte-identical, including a g12v2.role clause about G12 v4 that has gone stale; and the absence of a finding-disposition block, which after three turns and seven accumulated advisories is the thing I would most like to see if a v4 is ever authored for another reason. It is not a reason to author one. This ACCEPT does not dispose of the competing v1 reviews; that remains yours.
